loText: Compare various money market and capital market instruments and discuss their advantages and disadvantages.
question:
A junior risk analyst at a US bank is estimating the federal income tax that arises this year on the price gains (not the coupon interest) of two municipal bonds. Taxable gains are taxed at the bank’s 35% marginal rate.

| Bond | Par (USD m) | Purchase | Value received | Coupon (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P | 30 | At issue, at a discounted price of 95.50 | 100.00 | 3.2 |
| Q | 20 | At par, 100.00, in the secondary market | 104.25 | 4.0 |

Bond P was held to maturity and redeemed at par. Bond Q was sold after market rates fell. The bank funded both purchases with borrowings costing 5.1%. Which of the following is closest to the federal tax on the two bonds’ price gains?
solution:
Federal tax on the price gains of two municipal bonds: discount accretion versus market gain.

**Concept and theory**

The tax advantage of municipal bonds attaches to their interest, not to all of their income. GARP states that capital gains on municipals are fully taxable, with one exception: for bonds sold (issued) at a discounted price, the gain from the purchase price up to par value is treated as a portion of tax-exempt interest earnings. The logic is that a bond issued below par pays part of its interest in the form of the price rising to par, so that accretion is interest in substance and inherits the exemption. A gain caused by a fall in market rates that lifts the price above what was paid is a true capital gain and is taxed.

loText: Apply investment maturity strategies and maturity management tools based on the yield curve and duration.
question: A senior treasury analyst at a UK bank is preparing a board paper recommending the sale of GBP 400 million of unpledged gilts. Loan revenues are down this year, and the sale would realize a pre-tax loss of GBP 3.2 million. The board will approve a loss-making trade only if management shows that the loss will be more than made up by higher expected returns on the replacement assets. Which of the following is the least appropriate justification for the trade?

options.A: The house forecast is for rising interest rates, so the bank can lock in higher yields at the long end of the yield curve by extending maturities now.
options.B: The sale and reinvestment, combined with effective tax management, would raise the portfolio’s expected after-tax return.
options.C: The trade would improve overall asset quality, helping the bank better weather an economic downturn.
options.D: The portfolio could be moved toward higher-grade securities without an appreciable loss in expected return.

solution:
UK bank board paper: which justification for a loss-making securities sale is least appropriate?

**Concept and theory**

Trading securities before maturity is the operational side of the rate expectations approach. GARP notes that banks often trade some of their unpledged holdings whenever there is the prospect of significant gains in expected returns or the opportunity to reduce asset risk without significant loss in expected yield, and they are particularly aggressive when loan revenues are down. But losses on security trades reduce before-tax income, so portfolio managers do not like to take losses unless they can show the board that the loss will be more than made up by higher expected returns on the new assets bought with the proceeds.

loText: Compare strategies that a bank can use to meet demands for additional liquidity.
question: A junior risk analyst at a US savings institution is compiling notes on the principal sources of borrowed liquidity. Which of the following notes is most accurate?

options.A: Borrowing from the central bank’s discount window is usually available within minutes, provided the institution has collateral on hand and a signed borrowing authorization.
options.B: Repurchase agreements always carry a fixed interest rate and maturity, so a continuing-contract RP must be renegotiated with the lender every day.
options.C: Advances from the Federal Home Loan Bank system are available to any depository institution, regardless of whether it lends in the real-estate-backed loan market.
options.D: Eurocurrency deposits are issued at interest rates set by the central bank, rather than by the demand and supply for these short-term international deposits.

solution:
Which note on the principal sources of borrowed liquidity is accurate?

**Concept and theory**

GARP’s box “Borrowing Liquidity: The Principal Options” describes six sources a bank can tap when a liquidity deficit arises. Their features matter when comparing how quickly, at what price and under what conditions purchased liquidity can be obtained.

| Source | Key features (GARP 5.4) |
|---|---|
| Federal funds borrowings | Reserves from other lenders that can be accessed immediately |
| Repurchase agreements | Sale of liquid, low-risk securities to institutions with temporary surpluses; generally fixed rate and maturity, but continuing-contract RPs stay in force until either party terminates |
